name: GraphBase
tagline: FactNexus's commercial graph DBMS that treats whole graphs as transactional units for knowledge graphs.
description: GraphBase is a proprietary graph database from the Australian company FactNexus. Instead of a fixed property-graph or triple model it offers configurable lightweight primitives, so a single store can mix triple-store, property-graph and hypergraph structures; vertices hold objects with their arcs stored inside them, and an entire graph can be treated as a transactional unit that is cut, combined or copied. Queries 'bound' a sub-graph and return it, built either with visual drag-and-drop tools or through APIs, and Java handlers can run logic inside the database. FactNexus currently markets it as GraphBase Enterprise Cloud for knowledge graphs and retrieval-augmented generation. Public documentation, pricing and independent benchmarks are scarce, so evaluate it directly with the vendor.

pricing.notes: No public pricing; sold through FactNexus.

scale.notes: Vendor claims a single 1U server handles a graph of two billion vertices and 200 billion arcs; not independently verified.

strengths: Whole graphs can be copied, merged or cut as single transactional units
Mixes triple, property-graph and hypergraph structures in one store
Visual tools for building and running sub-graph queries
Java handlers run application logic inside the database
weaknesses: Very little public documentation, pricing or community
No standard query language such as Cypher, GQL or SPARQL
Performance claims come only from the vendor
notIdealFor: Teams that want open standards or open source
Projects needing a large hiring pool or community support
